elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph grants Customer only a licence ("grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables and products delivered hereunder"); nothing vests ownership of deliverables in Customer, and warranty (viii) still says Kubient is "the rightful owner or licensee of all intellectual property rights to the Service, the Auction Platform and products delivered hereunder".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; the redline deliberately elects the licence-back fallback instead.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools, know-how and the Auction Platform.", reinforced by retained warranty (viii).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The grant over "the deliverables and products delivered hereunder" is expressly "perpetual" and is broad enough to cover Kubient IP embedded in them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Grant is expressly "irrevocable"; the revocable Section 2 licence is a separate Auction Platform access licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: No sentence states that Customer retains ownership of or all rights in its Content/data; the new third sentence only caps Kubient's licence, and Section 6(a) merely allocates responsibility and liability for the Content.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Kubient in the Content or in any other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services." — covers every category of Customer data, not just named types.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No no-joint-ownership sentence was added; the document is silent on joint ownership.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: "Kubient retains ownership of its generic tools, know-how and the Auction Platform."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables and products delivered hereunder".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Word "irrevocable" appears in the new grant; the retained "revocable" licence in Section 2 is scoped to Auction Platform access, which warranty (viii) treats as distinct from "products delivered hereunder".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Word "worldwide" appears in the new grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Word "royalty-free" appears in the new grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables and products delivered hereunder for Customer's business"; Section 6(a)'s no-modification covenant is limited to "any software included in any Service", not to products delivered hereunder.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "sublicense ... for Customer's business"; Section 2's "without right of sublicense" applies only to the hosted Auction Platform access licence.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Third inserted sentence limits any Kubient licence in "the Content or in any other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer" to "processing it solely to provide the Services"; no residual resale/independent-exploitation right is granted.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Not a preferred-level element; listed only for completeness — the equivalent preferred element (pre-existing IP retention) is assessed above as met.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: one inserted paragraph supplies Vendor retention of generic tools/know-how, a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense licence to deliverables and products delivered hereunder for Customer's business, and a solely-to-provide-the-Services limit on any Kubient licence in Customer Content and any other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer.

Preferred level fails on four elements: no Customer ownership of deliverables, no Vendor assignment, no sentence that Customer retains all rights in Customer Data, and no no-joint-ownership statement. If the preferred position is pursued, add (i) "Customer owns, and Kubient hereby assigns to Customer, all right, title and interest in the deliverables and work product created for Customer", (ii) "Customer retains all right, title and interest in the Content and all Customer data", and (iii) "No intellectual property will be jointly owned", and conform warranty (viii) accordingly.

Minimality holds: the change is a single concise insertion into a document with no IP article, deletes nothing, and adds no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural boilerplate. The only surplus is the words "and the Auction Platform" in the retention sentence, which concede more than the element requires and are already covered by warranty (viii) — they could be trimmed, but they are consistent with the playbook note that Vendor platform ownership is acceptable and do not disturb any Customer right.

Intent is preserved: nothing is assigned to Kubient, Section 2's revocable, non-sublicensable licence remains scoped to hosted Auction Platform access and Section 6(a)'s no-modify/no-resell covenants remain scoped to "any Service", both of which warranty (viii) treats as distinct from "products delivered hereunder", so no retained sentence directly contradicts the new grant. To remove all residual ambiguity the drafter may open the new sentence with "Notwithstanding Sections 2 and 6(a)," but that is optional and would slightly expand the edit.

"Deliverables" is used in lower case as ordinary language rather than as an undefined capitalised term, and "products delivered hereunder" tracks existing warranty (viii) wording, so no dangling defined term or cross-reference is created.
